name: contact-form-7
notes: DUO-3222 (version-pinned adapter compatibility contract): plugin/version_range verified live (not guessed) — contact-form-7/wp-contact-form-7.php, re-confirmed at 6.1.6 this session (unchanged from the R1-A grind round's own grounding below — same version, re-verified independently, not assumed stale-and-still-true). Range scoped to the CURRENT major line only (6.x, [6.0.0, 7.0.0)) — widening to cover other major versions is DUO-3224's ratification job, not invented here.

Grind R1-A: all 8 postmeta keys verified empirically against a real form created via WPCF7_ContactForm::get_template()+save() (CF7 6.1.6's own admin-screen code path, not hand-authored postmeta) and customized mail settings — every value is plain text/merge-tags or a nested object of plain text. _old_cf7_unit_id is the one deliberate alternate identity fact; it is resolved only through the declared post-meta/post-type locator, never as wp_posts.ID.

CF7 6.1.6's legacy formatter emits [contact-form <old_id> "<title>"], and the runtime resolves that positional integer through _old_cf7_unit_id. The positional shortcode_attrs rule canonicalizes that value to the form's post token in post bodies and structured string leaves (including Elementor payloads), then restores the target form's own alternate on apply; missing, duplicate, non-positive, non-decimal, or wrong-domain alternates refuse loudly.

_hash: a persisted per-form random opaque string (wpcf7_generate_contact_form_hash(), add_post_meta()'d once on first save, never regenerated) — NOT a secret (doesn't match Secrets::HARD_PATTERNS or the suspicious key-name heuristic) and NOT a ref. It matters structurally though: CF7's own shortcode embeds `id="<first 7 chars of _hash>"`, not the numeric post id — WPCF7_ContactForm::find()/hash lookup resolves the shortcode to whichever post currently holds that hash, fresh at every render. Confirmed empirically (grind round R1-A's round-trip): because _hash round-trips as ordinary opaque authored postmeta, a page's `[contact-form-7 id="..."]` shortcode text needs no rewriting at all and resolves correctly on a second environment even though the form's own numeric post id differs there — CF7's embedding is ref-safe by construction, unlike Ninja Forms' block/shortcode (see manifests/ninja-forms.json).

_form/_mail/_mail_2/_messages/_additional_settings/_locale: CF7's own save() path (contact-form.php save()) writes each contact-form 'property' as its own postmeta key via update_post_meta($post_id, '_'.$prop, ...) — _form is a plain string (the field markup), _mail/_mail_2 are nested arrays (recipient/subject/body/etc, all plain strings — the whole-structure string-leaf tokenizer handles them for free, same as any other authored nested value), _messages is a flat string map, _locale a locale code string, _additional_settings an opaque multi-line string. None observed to ever contain an id in this exploration.
The manifest declares the non-public wpcf7_contact_form post type so Capture can discover and gate CF7 forms; site.duo.json still controls the site's broader post_type scope.
